---
title: "Thicket-specific intensity refinement"
---

## Summary

Biome-specific ecosystem condition information is being tested as an additional source of land use intensity for BII segments classified as "Untransformed" within the Thicket biome.

A recent [project](https://vdmstephni.github.io/ecosystem_condition/content/thicket/) mapped degradation in the Thicket biome in South Africa, which is strongly associated with rangeland use intensity, particularly browsing by domestic livestock. Most of the biome is currently classified as Untransformed in BII, but the ecosystems have been heavily degraded by overutilisation of rangelands that occured prior to satellite monitoring started. Because Thicket vegetation does not renegerate naturally, the degradation can still be observed with remote sensing.

## Input data

Script: <https://code.earthengine.google.com/6756a26efc2945884f1b96c5ee0c0856>

-   National BII segment raster.
-   National BII land use reclassification.
-   National protected area layer.
-   Thicket biome boundaries:

``` text
projects/thicket-ecological-condition/assets/ThicketEFGs
```

-   Thicket degradation probability surfaces:

``` text
projects/thicket-ecological-condition/assets/RF_prob_surfaces_solid_thicket_2025
```

The probability raster contains:

``` text
p_intact = probability of being intact
p_moderate = probability of being moderately degraded
p_severe = = probability of being severely degraded
```

## Data preparation

The national segment workflow was clipped to the mapped Thicket biome extent.

The pixel-level Thicket intensity score was calculated as:

$$
I = 0.5p_{moderate} + p_{severe}
$$

This assigns the following class endpoints:

| Condition | Intensity contribution |
|-----------|-----------------------:|
| Intact    |                      0 |
| Moderate  |                    0.5 |
| Severe    |                      1 |

Only valid, unmasked probability pixels are used. Pixels masked in the probability raster were excluded from the condition model because they were already transformed, water or otherwise outside the modelled natural extent.

## Analysis

Valid pixel-level land use intensity scores were averaged within each segment. The Thicket-derived score is used only to refine the intensity of segments assigned to the Untransformed BII land use class. The dominant BII land use allocation remains unchanged. Transformed classes retain their national BII intensity rules.

Two protected area rules were initially compared:

1.  apply the Thicket intensity score to untransformed and protected segments; and

2.  retain protected areas at an intensity of 0.

The workflow will later be extended as equivalent biome-specific intensity datasets become available.
